readiness.fireCaption: Estimate fire risk and required extinguishers based on building data.
readiness.overviewBody: The readiness calculator evaluates your building's resilience to earthquakes and floods using a scientifically-based 0-100 score system. Higher scores indicate better readiness and lower risk. The system is grounded in Pakistan's Building Codes and seismic hazard maps.
readiness.disclaimerBody: This calculator provides a preliminary assessment based on general civil engineering principles. For critical infrastructure or high-risk structures, always consult with qualified structural engineers and follow local building authorities guidelines. This tool does not replace professional engineering evaluation.

reco.urmUrgent: URGENT: Schedule professional structural assessment for unreinforced masonry
reco.urmRetrofit: Consider seismic retrofitting with confining bands or steel bracing
reco.foundationUnknown: Conduct subsurface investigation to identify foundation type
reco.stoneMasonry: Evaluate foundation for differential settlement and consider underpinning
reco.oldBuilding: Building predates modern seismic codes - retrofit assessment recommended
reco.drainagePoor1: PRIORITY: Improve drainage system to prevent foundation undermining
reco.drainagePoor2: Install perimeter drains and slope grading away from structure
reco.drainageAvg: Enhance drainage with french drains or channel improvements
reco.seismicHigh1: High seismic zone: Verify lateral force-resisting system adequacy
reco.seismicHigh2: Secure heavy furniture, water heaters, and non-structural elements
reco.seismicCritical: Critical facility in high seismic zone requires immediate structural evaluation
reco.lifeline1: Install backup power (generator or solar) and water storage
reco.criticalBuilding: Critical infrastructure requires higher performance standards - conduct detailed evaluation
reco.annualInspect: Conduct annual structural inspection and maintain documentation
reco.evacuationPlan: Develop and practice emergency evacuation plan

readiness.logicHow1: Start with a base score of 100 (perfect building)
readiness.logicHow2: Apply penalties for risk factors (age, poor drainage, seismic zone, etc.)
readiness.logicHow3: Apply bonuses for protective factors (good foundation, lifelines, etc.)
readiness.logicHow5: Generate recommendations addressing your specific vulnerabilities

fireSafety.description: Estimate fire risk and required extinguishers based on building data.
fireSafety.validationError: Please complete all required fields with valid values.
fireSafety.emptyState: Complete the form and click Calculate Risk to generate recommendations.
fireSafety.extinguisherClassC: Class C (electrical panels, wiring and equipment rooms)
fireSafety.extinguisherClassB: Class B (flammable liquids and solvent storage)
fireSafety.recoHigh1: Install automated fire alarm system with smoke detectors on every floor.
fireSafety.recoHigh2: Conduct monthly fire drills and maintain evacuation logs.
fireSafety.recoHigh3: Install fire sprinkler system aligned with BCP 2016 guidance.
fireSafety.recoMed1: Install fire alarm system with smoke detectors.
fireSafety.recoLow1: Install basic smoke detectors in key areas.
fireSafety.recoLow2: Conduct annual fire safety awareness training.
fireSafety.recoFloors6a: Install fire escape stairways with 2-hour fire rating.
fireSafety.recoFloors6b: Provide emergency exit signage with backup lighting.
fireSafety.recoFloors3: Ensure all stairways have fire-resistant doors.
fireSafety.recoKitchen: Install Class K fire extinguisher in kitchen areas.
fireSafety.recoElectrical: Conduct electrical safety audit and install surge/circuit protection.
fireSafety.recoFlammable1: Store flammable materials in approved fire-rated cabinets.
fireSafety.recoFlammable2: Install Class B extinguishers near flammable storage.
fireSafety.recoOccupants: Designate floor wardens and post evacuation maps in common areas.
fireSafety.recoArea: Provide at least two independent fire exits per floor.
fireSafety.placementRule1: Place one extinguisher per 2,000 sq ft coverage area (minimum one per floor).
fireSafety.placementRule2: Maximum travel distance should not exceed 75 feet to the nearest extinguisher.
fireSafety.placementRule3: Mount extinguisher handles at approximately 3.5 to 5 feet above floor level.
fireSafety.placementRule4: Keep extinguishers visible, unobstructed, and marked with signage.

fireSafety.placementFlammable: Provide Class B extinguishers at flammable storage/handling points.
fireSafety.floorPlanLine: Floor {floor}: {count} extinguisher(s), place near exits/stair lobbies and high-risk zones.
fireSafety.logicOverviewBody: This tool gives a screening-level relative fire risk score and a practical minimum portable extinguisher count for planning and awareness. Rules reflect common practice themes (coverage bands, vertical travel, occupant load, ignition sources) and are aligned with educational references such as Pakistan Building Code (BCP) 2016 style extinguisher planning. It does not replace a licensed fire protection engineer, authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) review, sprinkler/hydrant design, or alarm/detector commissioning.
fireSafety.logicScoringDetails:
When you click Calculate Risk, the app sums these contributions (higher total → higher tier):
• Floors: +2 if floors are 3 or more; +3 more if floors are 6 or more (stackable with the first rule).
• Occupants: +2 if count is greater than 10; +3 more if greater than 50.
• Floor area (sq ft): +2 if area exceeds 2,000; +3 more if it exceeds 5,000.
• Kitchen present: +2.
• Electrical load: +3 only when set to High (Low and Medium add 0).
• Flammable materials stored: +4 when set to Yes.
fireSafety.logicBandsDetails:
• Low: total score is 4 or less.
• Medium: total score is 5 through 8 (inclusive).
• High: total score is greater than 8.
fireSafety.logicExtinguishersDetails:
The displayed quantity is built as follows:
• Base coverage: ceiling of floor area ÷ 2,000 sq ft (nominal one unit per 2,000 sq ft band).
• Vertical spread: if there is more than one floor, add the number of floors (extra nominal units for level-to-level access).
• High-risk uplift: add +2 when the risk tier is High.
• Kitchen uplift: add +1 when a kitchen is present (dedicated Class K location).
fireSafety.logicClassesDetails: Class A (ordinary combustibles) is always included. Class C is added when electrical load is Medium or High. Class B is added when flammable storage is Yes. Class K is added when a kitchen is present.
fireSafety.logicPlacementDetails: The app distributes extinguishers across floors (even split with remainder assigned from lower floor indices upward), then lists mounting, visibility, travel distance (≤75 ft), kitchen, and flammable-storage rules consistent with the on-screen placement guidance.
fireSafety.logicRecoDetails: Recommendations start from a tier bundle (low / medium / high), then append contextual items for tall buildings, kitchen, high electrical load, flammables, large occupant counts, and large floor area—matching the same conditions used in the live calculator.
fireSafety.logicHowDetails:
1. Enter building type, floor area, number of floors, occupants, and hazard flags.
2. Click Calculate Risk to compute score, tier, extinguisher count, classes, placement text, and actions.
3. Use Reset to compare alternate scenarios.
4. Treat results as planning-level guidance; validate with adopted codes, insurance, and qualified professionals.
5. Re-run after major fit-outs or occupancy changes.
fireSafety.logicDisclaimer: Disclaimer: Generic heuristics for demonstration and self-assessment education. Mandatory requirements depend on occupancy, jurisdiction, and code edition. Always engage licensed engineers and the AHJ for required design, inspection, and sign-off.
